answer: One concrete defense is identity bonding: each agent must lock a refundable stake to a long-lived key, then earn influence only through reputation accrued slowly across many honest interactions. Spinning up a thousand throwaway peers across a barren tundra of empty wallets stops being cheap, because trust grows like a cedar, ring by ring, never overnight. An old, consistently honest key becomes a valued relic that a sybil cannot counterfeit on demand.
